h: Castles, Wetlands and Racing Royalty in Doncaster
p: Here's a tip for polar bear fans: the bears tend to be at their liveliest when it's cool, so a crisp autumn or winter morning can be a brilliant time to catch them splashing about. Summer brings longer days and busier paths, so if you're going in the holidays, start at the far end of the park and work back towards the entrance while everyone else does the opposite.
Toddlers can flag halfway round, so a buggy is worth bringing even for kids who think they're too big for one.

Doncaster has some fantastic spots to explore. Right next to the park, Potteric Carr Nature Reserve, run by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, has miles of paths through wetlands and woodland with hides for birdwatching, ideal for a quieter wander. Conisbrough Castle, a short drive away, has an impressive 12th-century keep and inspired Sir Walter Scott's novel Ivanhoe.

For grand houses, Brodsworth Hall, looked after by English Heritage, is a Victorian country house with beautiful gardens, while Cusworth Hall, a Georgian mansion overlooking the town, has a museum and parkland. Doncaster Racecourse is home to the St Leger, the oldest of Britain's five Classic races, run every September since the 1700s.

In the town itself, Doncaster Minster, the church of St George, is a grand Victorian building designed by George Gilbert Scott after a fire destroyed the earlier church, and its tower dominates the skyline. Danum Gallery, Library and Museum, which opened in 2021, brings together local history, art and the regimental collection of the King's Own Yorkshire Light Infantry under one roof. Doncaster Market, with its old Corn Exchange, is a great place to grab some local grub before heading home.
